predecessors.name: Zhili clique
predecessors.text: Beijing, seized in the Beijing Coup of October 1924

successors.name: Republic of China
successors.text: 'what was left of the faction was absorbed into the KMT': Shaanxi, Gansu, Henan, Chahar and Suiyuan

ledger.x: November 1924 (bridging): 'It had control of much of Northwestern China, including Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan'; the Second Zhili-Fengtian War ended with 'a Zhili loss of all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun', and the Zhili clique held Chahar…
1925 (bridging): 'It had control of much of Northwestern China, including Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan'; the page gives no date and no former holder, so the year and the counterpart are readings.
1927: Feng Yuxiang takes the governorship of Gansu.
28 May 1927: the Guominjun takes Luoyang and Henan.
1928: the Guominjun joins the Northern Expedition.

December 1929 (bridging): the Cliopatria row changes from Kuomintang to Republic of China and the Nanjing government continues under the second name; the Northern Expedition page says only that after October 1928 'Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun continued to control Shaanxi, Henan, and parts of Shantung and Zhili' and is…
1930 (bridging): the Guominjun continues as a Nationalist ally under the Republic of China row until the Central Plains War.
May 1930: the alliance breaks in the Central Plains War.

wars.name: Second Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Anti-Zhili alliance victory; Feng Yuxiang's coup on 22/23 October 1924 decided it.

wars.name: Anti-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Defeat of the Guominjun by the Zhili-Fengtian alliance in January 1926: loss of Beijing and retreat to Zhangjiakou.

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Kuomintang victory: the Guominjun 'moved first, leaving their base in Shaanxi to march on Luoyang, in Henan' and took it on 28 May 1927, forcing Zhang Zongchang back to Shandong and Zhang Xueliang north of the Yellow River; Feng aligned with Nanjing in June…

wars.name: Central Plains War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the Northwest Army collapsed and Feng and Yan resigned on 4 November 1930; what was left of the faction was absorbed into the Kuomintang.

certainty.note: No boundaries on the pages; the north-west is the page's own list of provinces and the shapes are provinces and rings.
